description: Timeline comparison of how brands shifted ad budgets away from traditional TV into streaming video—and how that scramble reshaped the ad market. Includes major platform milestones and measurable revenue/estimates through 2025, plus 2026 projections.

entities.name: Traditional TV Advertising Spend (US Linear TV)

youtube_description:
🎬 Chaptered story: how ad dollars fled traditional linear TV and poured into streaming—and why it became a winner-take-most fight.

0:00 — The pre-streaming baseline (2007): linear TV owns the screen.
1:10 — 2010–2015: YouTube/online video normalizes viewing, but ad spend is still mostly TV.
2:35 — 2017–2019: Streaming formats mature; measurement and targeting improve—spend starts to bend.
3:55 — 2020: Pandemic viewing accelerates; streaming ad inventory grows faster than budgets.
5:10 — 2021–2022: Linear share keeps slipping; streaming ad spend keeps compounding.
6:25 — 2023–2024: Brands demand addressability and performance; ad tech tightens the race.
7:40 — 2025: The shift is no longer a trend—it’s the default allocation.
8:30 — 2026 (estimate projection): streaming climbs again while linear continues to erode.

📌 What you’ll see in the chart race:
• Linear TV declines from about $98B (2007) to ~$39B by 2026.
• Streaming ads rise from near-zero to ~$149B by 2026.
• Netflix and Amazon Advertising show how “where attention goes” turns into “where money goes.”

✅ Like & subscribe for more chart-race timelines—and comment which year you think the ad shift became irreversible.

Hashtags: #streaming #advertising #adtech #tv #chartrace #marketing #netflix #amazon #mediaindustry #digitalvideo
instagram_caption:
🚀 The Ad Exodus Nobody Could Stop

For years, TV was the “set it and forget it” ad machine. In 2007, traditional linear TV advertising in the US sat around **$98B**—the scoreboard everyone watched, the cash register everyone trusted.

Then the viewing habits changed faster than the ad contracts. By **2010**, linear TV was still near **$97B**, but streaming was already starting to form as a real channel—streaming ad spend was about **$8B**. By **2013**, linear slid to roughly **$92B**, while streaming ads climbed to **$18B**. The turning point wasn’t one announcement—it was years of incremental budget rerouting.

In **2017**, the gap looked like **$83B** linear versus about **$45B** streaming ads. But the real drama hit in **2020**: as screen time exploded, streaming ad inventory and targeting scaled under pressure. Linear TV fell to about **$71B**, while streaming ads jumped to **$69B**—and the race was officially on.

By **2022**, the “exodus” became visible in the numbers: linear TV was around **$58B**, while streaming ads were roughly **$93B**. And as measurement got sharper and performance mattered more than branding alone, streaming kept running. In **2025**, linear TV is estimated near **$41B**, while streaming ads reach about **$133B**. The 2026 projection pushes it further: **~$39B linear** vs **~$149B streaming ads**.

Meanwhile, the platforms reflected the money gravity. **Netflix revenue** rises from about **$6B (2007)** to roughly **$40B (2025)** (estimate), and **Amazon Advertising** grows from near-zero to about **$71B (2025)** (estimate), illustrating where advertisers chased both attention and outcomes.

🔥 So here’s your question: what do you think caused the biggest inflection—the **measurement shift**, the **targeting tech**, or the **audience behavior change**? Drop your pick below.
